refTraining.title: Training
refTraining.subtitle: Step-by-step walkthroughs of everything a referral partner does on this platform.
refTraining.gettingStartedTitle: Getting started: your Referral Program Dashboard
refTraining.gettingStartedDesc: What each box on your dashboard is for, and where to begin.
refTraining.gettingStartedStep1: Open the Referral Program Dashboard from the sidebar — it is your home screen as a partner.
refTraining.gettingStartedStep2: Use the Clients box to add the companies you introduce and to track where each one has reached.
refTraining.gettingStartedStep3: Use Marketing Tools to send an introduction that already carries your discount code.
refTraining.gettingStartedStep4: Use Credit Earned to see what you have made, and Sales Generated to see what your clients have paid.
refTraining.addClientDesc: Register a company you are introducing so the referral is credited to you.
refTraining.addClientStep1: Open the Clients screen and press Add Client.
refTraining.addClientStep2: Enter the contact person’s first and last name and the email address you will write to.
refTraining.addClientStep3: Add the company name so the proposal letter can address the organisation rather than the person.
refTraining.addClientStep4: Add a WhatsApp number and website if you have them — both are optional.
refTraining.addClientStep5: Save, and the client appears in your table linked to your partner account.
refTraining.sendInviteDesc: The introduction letter that carries your discount code to the client.
refTraining.sendInviteStep1: Find the client in your Clients table — invites are sent from the row itself.
refTraining.sendInviteStep2: Press Send Invite on that row.
refTraining.sendInviteStep3: The letter goes out from Certify.cx with your discount code already inside it, so you write and attach nothing.
refTraining.sendInviteStep4: The row updates to show the invite was sent, so you can see who is still waiting to hear from you.
refTraining.sendProposalDesc: The formal proposal letter, with the company profile and the standard’s brochure attached.
refTraining.sendProposalStep1: Open Marketing Tools and choose the client you are writing to.
refTraining.sendProposalStep2: Choose the ISO standard the proposal is about.
refTraining.sendProposalStep3: Tick whether to attach the company profile, the standard’s brochure, or both.
refTraining.sendProposalStep4: Say whether the company already holds a certification — the letter is worded differently if it does.
refTraining.sendProposalStep5: Press Send now. The letter leaves under the Certify.cx name with your discount code inside it.
refTraining.discountCodeTitle: Your discount code and referral link
refTraining.discountCodeDesc: How a client is tied to you, and what your code gives them.
refTraining.discountCodeStep1: Open Coupons to share to see the code and referral link issued to you.
refTraining.discountCodeStep2: Your code gives the client a discount on their certification fee, so it is a reason for them to use it.
refTraining.discountCodeStep3: Share it by sending the invitation email, or copy the link into your own message.
refTraining.discountCodeStep4: When a client buys using your code or link, the sale is credited to you and your commission is calculated from it.
refTraining.commissionsDesc: When you earn, how your rate rises, and how you get paid.
refTraining.commissionsStep1: Open Credit Earned to see every referred client and what each one has earned you.
refTraining.commissionsStep2: A commission is credited once the client has paid for their certification, not when they are invited.
refTraining.commissionsStep3: Your rate rises as you bring in more paid clients — your current tier and the next one are shown on the same screen.
refTraining.commissionsStep4: Commission that has been paid out and commission still owed are listed separately, so you always know what is outstanding.

investorCampaigns.spamDisclaimer: What these numbers can't tell you: whether a delivered email landed in someone's spam/junk folder. No email provider — not Resend, not Gmail, not anyone — can see inside a recipient's own mailbox. Bounces and spam complaints (above) are the real, trackable signal of deliverability health.
